steps.title: Import TypeScript types and interfaces
steps.instruction: Create a new TypeScript file and define your own types and interfaces for this lesson. We'll start by creating a simple interface for a workflow node.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword to define a TypeScript interface. You don't need to import anything yet - we're creating our own types.
steps.seedCode: // Create your TypeScript types and interfaces here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript file with at least one interface defined for a workflow node.
successCriteria: A TypeScript interface named 'WorkflowNode' is defined with properties for a workflow graph node
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a TypeScript interface for workflow nodes. This is the foundation for our typed finite workflow graph.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined an interface with properties that could represent a workflow node (like id, name, or status).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword followed by a name and property definitions in curly braces.

steps.title: Define Node interface for workflow states
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Node' with three properties: 'id' (string), 'label' (string), and 'type' (string).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with type annotations.
steps.seedCode:
// Create your TypeScript types and interfaces here

// Define Node interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Node interface is created with the required typed properties.
successCriteria: The Node interface is defined with id: string, label: string, and type: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Node interface with proper TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your Node interface has all three required properties with correct string type annotations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Node interface definition is missing or incorrect. Please define an interface named Node with id, label, and type properties, all typed as string.

steps.title: Define Edge interface for transitions
steps.instruction: Define an Edge interface with source, target, and label properties. Make all properties required strings.
steps.hint: Create an interface named Edge with three properties: source, target, and label, all typed as string.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a typed Edge interface representing transitions between workflow states.
successCriteria: An Edge interface is defined with source, target, and label properties, all typed as string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your Edge interface correctly defines the transition structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that all three properties (source, target, label) are present and typed as strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Edge interface is missing or incorrect. Ensure you define an interface named Edge with three string properties.

steps.title: Define WorkflowGraph type
steps.instruction: Create a WorkflowGraph type that contains nodes and edges arrays, using the Node and Edge interfaces you defined earlier.
steps.hint: Define a new type alias with the 'type' keyword that has two properties: nodes (array of Node) and edges (array of Edge).
steps.expectedOutcome: A WorkflowGraph type is defined, combining the Node and Edge interfaces into a complete graph structure.
successCriteria: The WorkflowGraph type is defined with nodes and edges properties, both typed as arrays of the respective interfaces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the WorkflowGraph type, creating a complete structure for your workflow graph.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your WorkflowGraph type includes both nodes and edges properties with the correct array types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The WorkflowGraph type definition is missing or incorrect. It should have nodes (Node[]) and edges (Edge[]) properties.

steps.title: Create sample workflow data
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'sampleWorkflow' that implements the WorkflowGraph type with sample data.
steps.hint: Define a constant with the WorkflowGraph type, providing arrays of nodes and edges that match your interface definitions.
steps.expectedOutcome: A constant 'sampleWorkflow' is defined with the WorkflowGraph type, containing sample nodes and edges.
successCriteria: The constant 'sampleWorkflow' is declared with the WorkflowGraph type and contains valid arrays of nodes and edges.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created typed sample data that matches your WorkflowGraph structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Ensure 'sampleWorkflow' is typed as WorkflowGraph and contains both nodes and edges arrays.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constant 'sampleWorkflow' is missing or doesn't match the WorkflowGraph type. Review the interface definitions.

steps.title: Create NodeDisplay component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named NodeDisplay that accepts a single prop of type Node. The component should return a <div> element containing the node's label.
steps.hint: Define the component with proper TypeScript typing for its props. Use the Node interface you created earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NodeDisplay component that renders a node's label in a div element.
successCriteria: NodeDisplay component is defined with proper TypeScript props typing and returns JSX containing the node label.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed React component that accepts a Node prop and displays its label.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component accepts a prop of type Node and returns JSX containing the node's label.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't meet the requirements. Check that you're using the Node interface for props and returning JSX with the label.

steps.title: Create EdgeDisplay component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named EdgeDisplay that accepts a single prop of type Edge and returns a paragraph element displaying the edge's source, target, and label.
steps.hint: Define a component with props typed as { edge: Edge } and return JSX showing the edge details.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new EdgeDisplay component is defined with proper TypeScript typing for its props.
successCriteria: EdgeDisplay component exists, accepts an edge prop of type Edge, and returns a paragraph showing edge details.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed EdgeDisplay component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but check that it accepts an edge prop with the correct type and returns the expected JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The EdgeDisplay component is missing or doesn't match the required structure. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Create WorkflowGraphVisualizer component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named WorkflowGraphVisualizer that takes a WorkflowGraph as props and returns a wrapper div element.
steps.hint: Define a component with props typed as WorkflowGraph and return a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A WorkflowGraphVisualizer component is defined with typed props and returns a div element.
successCriteria: The WorkflowGraphVisualizer component is created with proper TypeScript props typing and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the WorkflowGraphVisualizer component with typed props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your component accepts WorkflowGraph props and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. Check that you've defined a component named WorkflowGraphVisualizer with typed props and a return statement.

steps.title: Render the sample workflow
steps.instruction: In your component, pass the sampleWorkflow data as a prop to the WorkflowGraphVisualizer component.
steps.hint: Look for the WorkflowGraphVisualizer component you created earlier and pass sampleWorkflow to it using the appropriate prop name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: passing data to a component
<DisplayData data={myData} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The WorkflowGraphVisualizer component receives the sampleWorkflow data and renders it.
successCriteria: sampleWorkflow is passed as a prop to WorkflowGraphVisualizer.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully passed the typed workflow data to the visualizer component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're passing sampleWorkflow as a prop to WorkflowGraphVisualizer.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to pass the sampleWorkflow data to the WorkflowGraphVisualizer component.

steps.title: Add type safety validation
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateWorkflow that takes a WorkflowGraph parameter and returns a boolean indicating whether the graph structure is valid.
steps.hint: Check that all edges reference existing node IDs from the nodes array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateWorkflow function that checks edge references against node IDs.
successCriteria: The validateWorkflow function is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added runtime type validation to ensure workflow graphs are structurally sound.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function has the correct signature and validation logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function is missing or doesn't match the expected structure. Try implementing a function that validates edge references.
